title: Kinetic energy scaling
statement:
Speed triples while mass stays fixed. What happens to the kinetic energy?

[_]{a}

explanations: This would be linear in speed.
This reverses the effect of increasing speed.
Mass alone does not set kinetic energy.

hints: Square the ratio of the speeds.
solution: Because $KE=mv^2/2$, tripling speed multiplies the kinetic energy by nine.
